title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff + regional failover ordering
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: production incident on 2025-11-10 exposed two related instability modes in the SLO enforcement path: (1) backoff ordering inversion during concurrent regional failover decisions which caused thrashing between regions; (2) aggressive load-shedding that dropped emerging prefix-cached requests and increased tail latency for critical API routes. Motivation: reduce outage surface and ensure graceful degradation under regional capacity pressure. This PR applies a focused hotfix that preserves request ordering during regional failover, introduces a stable backoff comparator for the SLO enforcer, and relaxes load-shedding heuristics for in-flight cached prefixes. Changes are conservative and covered by unit and targeted integration tests. Checklist: - [x] Add comparator that orders failover/backoff decisions by (priority, timestamp, fail_count) to prevent reordering races - [x] Ensure in-flight KV cache pointers are retained when a request is re-routed to fallback region - [x] Add metric 'slo_enforcer.failover_reorders' and histogram for backoff delays - [x] Relax prefix-preserving load-shedding threshold for customer routes (route_tag:critical=true) - [x] Add regression tests for regional ordering and load-shedding behavior - [x] Run canary in us-west-2 for 2 hours before global rollout Impact: reduces failover-induced thrashing and improves tail latency for high-priority customer routes. Rollout: canary -> gradual 10% increments over 3 hours -> full rollout if canary is clean. Related: ENG-4821 (incident postmortem), SUP-9142 (customer support ticket).

Lina Gomez: Are there cases where preserving the KV pointer could leak memory or hold a goroutine? Please ensure we nullify references after reroute.
Aisha Patel: Good catch - added explicit nullify and lifecycle comment; unit tests assert no pointer retention post-completion.
